1	# PROGRAM.md — the live research program
2	
3	This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
4	Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
5	it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
6	`experiments/` and `novel/`.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
11	π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.
12	
13	**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
14	approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
15	theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
16	GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
17	mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
18	honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
19	with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
20	adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.
21	
22	## ACTIVE LINE — the verification program (started S491, 2026-06-13)

24	Computation of π(x) is blocked at √x; *verification* is not. Built and
25	measured (all unconditionally sound, all with cheating-prover tests):

28	|---|---|---|---|

# PROGRAM.md — the live research program

This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
`experiments/` and `novel/`.

## Goal

An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.

**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.

## ACTIVE LINE — the verification program (started S491, 2026-06-13)

Computation of π(x) is blocked at √x; *verification* is not. Built and
measured (all unconditionally sound, all with cheating-prover tests):

| protocol | verifies | verifier | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| wheel sum-check | Φ(x, polylog wheel) | polylog | done |
| Lucy base | exact π(x) | Õ(x/log x) | done — π(2²⁰−1) verified |
| Lucy + delegated wiring | exact π(x) | **Õ(√x)** | done — crossover p≈130 measured |
| compressed-prover mult-trace (step 1) | batched `Σ_d eq(ρ,d)S̃(⌊X/(dp)⌋)` | polylog `O(m·Lv)` | done — trace-certified quotient, 6 cheat classes rejected |
| compressed Lucy layer (step 2) | one large-side layer over the √x state | polylog + O(nb·p) wiring | done — affine/trace dispatch, 5 cheat classes, outputs = true MLEs |
| compressed two-sided chain (step 3) | **exact π(x) over the √x state, all K layers** | Õ(√x) (waff O(nb·p) undelegated) | done — π(x)=sieve at n≤16; 9+3 cheat classes incl. self-consistent liar |
| compressed chain + delegated wiring (step 4) | same, **both wirings delegated** | **cleanly Õ(√x)**, O(nb·log p)/layer, no p-linear term | done — π(x)=sieve at n≤16; 13 cheat classes incl. 4 delegation-specific liars |
| structured chain prover (step 5) | same, **prover Õ(x)** not Õ(x^{3/2}) | unchanged Õ(√x) | done — bit-identical transcript; prover/chain-layer O(p²)→O(p), ratio→44× @p=1021 |
| structured prover IN the compressed chain (step 6) | same, on the REAL compressed √x-state chain | unchanged Õ(√x) | done — `--structured` threaded through `compressed_layer.py`; bit-identical (selftest 15); `--prover-bench` ratio→46× @p=1021, both wirings |

Canonical doc: `novel/succinct_verification_of_pi.md` (protocol stack,

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	lucy_dp_verification.py — interactive proof for the EXACT value of pi(x).
4	
5	An untrusted prover runs the Lucy_Hedgehog / Legendre sieve DP and then
6	convinces a verifier of the exact value of pi(x) with UNCONDITIONAL
7	(information-theoretic) soundness. The verifier checks every layer of
8	the DP recursion via sum-check without ever sieving, touching only
9	O(n)-size objects per layer plus an O(n*p) automaton evaluation for the
10	floor-division wiring.
11	
12	Protocol (new object, S491). State function after sieving by the first
13	i primes, defined for ALL v in [0, 2^n):
14	
15	    S_0(v) = max(v - 1, 0)                       (count of 2..v)
16	    S_i(v) = S_{i-1}(v) - b_i(v) * (S_{i-1}(floor(v/p_i)) - (i-1))
17	
18	where b_i(v) = [v >= p_i^2]. The recurrence holds pointwise for every v
19	(Lucy_Hedgehog), and S_K(x) = pi(x) once K = pi(sqrt(x)). Crucially
20	S_{i-1}(p_i - 1) = i - 1 is a PUBLIC constant (the primes below p_i),
21	so each layer's correction scalar needs no extra claim.
22	
23	Per layer i (claim: tilde{S_i}(z) = C):
24	  Phase A  (n rounds, degree <= 3): sum-check of
25	      C = sum_v eq(z,v) * [ S(v) - B(v) * (G(v) - (i-1)) ]
26	    with G(v) := S_{i-1}(floor(v/p_i)) as an independent table; ends
27	    with prover claims s1 = tilde{S}(r_v), g1 = tilde{G}(r_v); verifier
28	    evaluates eq(z, r_v) in O(n) and tilde{B}(r_v) by a 3-state
29	    comparator automaton in O(n), and checks the combination.
30	  Phase B  (n rounds, degree <= 2): sum-check of
31	      g1 = sum_u W(r_v, u) * S(u),   W(v,u) = [u = floor(v/p_i)]
32	    ends with claim s2 = tilde{S}(r_u); verifier evaluates
33	    tilde{W}(r_v, r_u) by the LONG-DIVISION AUTOMATON: p states
34	    (the running remainder), reading bits of v MSB-first and emitting
35	    the quotient bits of u — O(n*p) per layer. This is the structured-
36	    wiring primitive that makes the verifier sublinear.
37	  Line batching: the two claims s1@r_v, s2@r_u about tilde{S_{i-1}}
38	    reduce to one claim at a random point on the line through them
39	    (prover sends the degree-<=n restriction).
40	Base layer: tilde{S_0}(z) = Int(z) - 1 + prod_j (1 - z_j), a closed
41	form the verifier evaluates in O(n). Int(z) = sum_j 2^{n-1-j} z_j.
42	
43	Costs: prover O~(K * 2^n) here (table-based demo; a production prover
44	works on the O(sqrt x)-size compressed Lucy table). Verifier
45	O(n * sum_{p <= sqrt x} p) field ops with the automaton wiring;
46	communication O(K * n) field elements. Soundness error <= ~7nK/q,
47	unconditional. Field q = 2^31 - 1 for numpy-exact arithmetic (a
48	production protocol lifts to q ~ 2^61 or an extension field).
49	
50	What would falsify this construction: an accepted honest run whose
51	output differs from a direct sieve's pi(x); a cheating prover (wrong
52	claim, adaptive round patching, or a corrupted DP table propagated
53	consistently downstream) accepted at a rate above the soundness bound;
54	or verifier work scaling with 2^n instead of n * sum p.
55	
56	Usage:
57	  python3 lucy_dp_verification.py --selftest
58	  python3 lucy_dp_verification.py --n 16 --cheat-trials 25
59	"""
60	
61	import argparse
62	import time
63	
64	import numpy as np
65	
66	Q = (1 << 31) - 1
67	
68	
69	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
70	# small field helpers
71	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
72	
73	def lagrange_eval(ys, r):
74	    """Evaluate the polynomial through (j, ys[j]), j = 0..deg, at r."""
75	    k = len(ys) - 1
76	    r = int(r) % Q
77	    total = 0
78	    for i in range(k + 1):
79	        num, den = 1, 1
80	        for j in range(k + 1):
81	            if j == i:
82	                continue
83	            num = (num * ((r - j) % Q)) % Q
84	            den = (den * ((i - j) % Q)) % Q
85	        total = (total + ys[i] * num % Q * pow(den, Q - 2, Q)) % Q
86	    return total
87	
88	
89	def eq_table(z):
90	    """Table of eq~(z, w) over Boolean w; index bit j (MSB-first) pairs
91	    with z[j]. PROVER-side object: O(2^n)."""
92	    t = np.array([1], dtype=np.uint64)
93	    for zj in reversed([int(v) % Q for v in z]):
94	        a = (t * ((Q + 1 - zj) % Q)) % Q
95	        b = (t * zj) % Q
96	        t = np.concatenate([a, b])
97	    return t
98	
99	
100	def eq_point(a, b):
101	    """eq~(a, b) for two field points. VERIFIER: O(n)."""
102	    acc = 1
103	    for x, y in zip(a, b):
104	        x, y = int(x) % Q, int(y) % Q
105	        acc = acc * ((x * y + (Q + 1 - x) * (Q + 1 - y)) % Q) % Q
106	    return acc
107	
108	
109	def mle_eval(table, pt):
110	    """tilde{table}(pt). PROVER-side: O(2^n)."""
111	    return int((table * eq_table(pt) % Q).sum(dtype=np.uint64) % Q)
112	
113	
114	def int_of_point(z):
115	    """Int(z) = sum_j 2^{n-1-j} z_j mod Q (degree-1 extension of the
116	    bits-to-integer map)."""
117	    n = len(z)
118	    return sum((1 << (n - 1 - j)) % Q * (int(z[j]) % Q) for j in range(n)) % Q
119	
120	
121	def s0_closed_form(z):
122	    """tilde{S_0}(z) = Int(z) - 1 + prod_j(1 - z_j). VERIFIER: O(n)."""
123	    prod = 1
124	    for zj in z:
125	        prod = prod * ((Q + 1 - int(zj)) % Q) % Q
126	    return (int_of_point(z) - 1 + prod) % Q
127	
128	
129	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# verifier-side automaton evaluations (the structured-wiring primitives)
131	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
132	
133	def ge_const_eval(rv, M, n):
134	    """MLE of [v >= M] at point rv. 3-state comparator (equal-so-far /
135	    greater / less), bits MSB-first. VERIFIER: O(n)."""
136	    st = [1, 0, 0]
137	    for j in range(n):
138	        mj = (M >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1
139	        w = [(Q + 1 - int(rv[j])) % Q, int(rv[j]) % Q]
140	        new = [0, 0, 0]
141	        for a in (0, 1):
142	            if a == mj:
143	                new[0] += st[0] * w[a]
144	            elif a > mj:
145	                new[1] += st[0] * w[a]
146	            else:
147	                new[2] += st[0] * w[a]
148	            new[1] += st[1] * w[a]
149	            new[2] += st[2] * w[a]
150	        st = [x % Q for x in new]
151	    return (st[0] + st[1]) % Q
152	
153	
154	def w_div_eval(rv, ru, p, n):
155	    """MLE of W(v, u) = [u = floor(v/p)] at (rv, ru). Long-division
156	    automaton: state = running remainder (< p); reading bit a of v
157	    MSB-first from state s gives t = 2s + a, emits quotient bit
158	    floor(t/p) and moves to t mod p. VERIFIER: O(n*p)."""
159	    st = [0] * p
160	    st[0] = 1
161	    for j in range(n):
162	        wv = [(Q + 1 - int(rv[j])) % Q, int(rv[j]) % Q]
163	        wu = [(Q + 1 - int(ru[j])) % Q, int(ru[j]) % Q]
164	        new = [0] * p
165	        for s in range(p):
166	            if st[s] == 0:
167	                continue
168	            for a in (0, 1):
169	                t = 2 * s + a
170	                b, s2 = divmod(t, p)
171	                new[s2] = (new[s2] + st[s] * wv[a] % Q * wu[b]) % Q
172	        st = new
173	    return sum(st) % Q
174	
175	
176	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
177	# generic sum-check over products of multilinear tables
178	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
179	
180	def sumcheck(claim, tables, terms, degree, rng, patch=False):
181	    """Sum-check for  claim = sum_w  sum_terms coef * prod tables[name][w].
182	    tables: dict name -> uint64 array (consumed). Interleaved prover
183	    (round polynomials by table halving) and verifier (consistency
184	    checks, random challenges). patch=True simulates an adaptive
185	    cheating prover that fixes up g(0) each round to mask a false claim.
186	    Returns (ok, r_list, final_claim, bound_scalars)."""
187	    nvars = int(np.log2(len(next(iter(tables.values())))))
188	    rs = []
189	    c = int(claim) % Q
190	    for _ in range(nvars):
191	        evals = []
192	        for X in range(degree + 1):
193	            xf = X % Q
194	            xc = (Q + 1 - X) % Q
195	            tot = 0
196	            for coef, names in terms:
197	                prod = None
198	                for nm in names:
199	                    tb = tables[nm]
200	                    h = len(tb) >> 1
201	                    row = (tb[:h] * xc + tb[h:] * xf) % Q
202	                    prod = row if prod is None else (prod * row) % Q
203	                tot = (tot + (coef % Q) * int(prod.sum(dtype=np.uint64) % Q)) % Q
204	            evals.append(tot)
205	        if patch:
206	            deficit = (c - (evals[0] + evals[1])) % Q
207	            evals[0] = (evals[0] + deficit) % Q
208	        # verifier checks and challenges
209	        if (evals[0] + evals[1]) % Q != c:
210	            return False, rs, None, None
211	        r = int(rng.integers(0, Q))
212	        rs.append(r)
213	        c = lagrange_eval(evals, r)
214	        # bind the variable in all tables
215	        rc = (Q + 1 - r) % Q
216	        for nm in tables:
217	            tb = tables[nm]
218	            h = len(tb) >> 1
219	            tables[nm] = (tb[:h] * rc + tb[h:] * r) % Q
220	    scalars = {nm: int(tables[nm][0]) for nm in tables}
221	    return True, rs, c, scalars
222	
223	
224	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
225	# the layered protocol
226	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
227	
228	def prover_tables(n, primes):
229	    """Prover precomputes all DP layers S_0..S_K (exact integers)."""
230	    N = 1 << n
231	    v = np.arange(N, dtype=np.int64)
232	    S = [np.maximum(v - 1, 0)]
233	    for i, p in enumerate(primes, start=1):
234	        prev = S[-1]
235	        b = v >= p * p
236	        upd = prev - b * (prev[v // p] - (i - 1))
237	        S.append(upd)
238	    return S
239	
240	
241	def verify_layer(i, p, n, z, claim, S_prev_field, rng, stats,
242	                 patch=False):
243	    """One layer reduction: claim about tilde{S_i}(z) -> claim about
244	    tilde{S_{i-1}} at a single new point. Returns (ok, new_z, new_claim)."""
245	    N = 1 << n
246	    v = np.arange(N, dtype=np.int64)
247	    c_i = (i - 1) % Q
248	
249	    # ---- prover builds phase-A tables (O(2^n)) ----
250	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
251	    EQ = eq_table(z)
252	    Sf = S_prev_field.copy()
253	    Bf = (v >= p * p).astype(np.uint64)
254	    Gf = S_prev_field[v // p]
255	    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
256	
257	    termsA = [(1, ["EQ", "S"]), (Q - 1, ["EQ", "B", "G"]),
258	              (c_i, ["EQ", "B"])]
259	    okA, r_v, finalA, scal = sumcheck(claim, {"EQ": EQ, "S": Sf, "B": Bf,
260	                                              "G": Gf}, termsA, 3, rng,
261	                                      patch=patch)
262	    if not okA:
263	        return False, None, None
264	    s1, g1 = scal["S"], scal["G"]  # prover claims
265	
266	    # ---- verifier-side phase-A final check (O(n)) ----
267	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
268	    eqv = eq_point(z, r_v)
269	    bv = ge_const_eval(r_v, p * p, n)
270	    expect = eqv * ((s1 - bv * ((g1 - c_i) % Q)) % Q) % Q
271	    ok = (finalA % Q) == expect
272	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
273	    if not ok:
274	        return False, None, None
275	
276	    # ---- phase B: verify g1 against the division wiring ----
277	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
278	    Wt = np.zeros(N, dtype=np.uint64)
279	    np.add.at(Wt, v // p, eq_table(r_v))   # sums of < p terms < Q each
280	    Wt %= Q
281	    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
282	
283	    okB, r_u, finalB, scalB = sumcheck(g1, {"W": Wt,
284	                                            "S": S_prev_field.copy()},
285	                                       [(1, ["W", "S"])], 2, rng,
286	                                       patch=patch)
287	    if not okB:
288	        return False, None, None
289	    s2 = scalB["S"]
290	
291	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
292	    wv = w_div_eval(r_v, r_u, p, n)
293	    ok = (finalB % Q) == wv * s2 % Q
294	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
295	    if not ok:
296	        return False, None, None
297	
298	    # ---- line batching: s1@r_v, s2@r_u -> one claim ----
299	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
300	    line_pts = []
301	    for t in range(n + 1):
302	        tf = t % Q
303	        gpt = [((Q + 1 - tf) * int(a) + tf * int(b)) % Q
304	               for a, b in zip(r_v, r_u)]
305	        line_pts.append(gpt)
306	    hs = [mle_eval(S_prev_field, gp) for gp in line_pts]  # prover
307	    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
308	
309	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
310	    if hs[0] != s1 or hs[1] != s2:   # verifier checks endpoints
311	        stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
312	        return False, None, None
313	    tstar = int(rng.integers(0, Q))
314	    new_claim = lagrange_eval(hs, tstar)
315	    tf = tstar % Q
316	    new_z = [((Q + 1 - tf) * int(a) + tf * int(b)) % Q
317	             for a, b in zip(r_v, r_u)]
318	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
319	    stats["comm"] += (4 * n) + (3 * n) + (n + 1) + 2  # field elems sent
320	    return True, new_z, new_claim
321	
322	
323	def run_protocol(n, rng, patch=False, corrupt_layer=None):
324	    """Full chain: verify pi(2^n - 1). Returns dict with outcome.
325	    corrupt_layer=i: prover corrupts one entry of S_i and recomputes
326	    all later layers consistently (a 'self-consistent liar')."""
327	    x = (1 << n) - 1
328	    primes = [p for p in range(2, int(x ** 0.5) + 1)
329	              if all(p % d for d in range(2, int(p ** 0.5) + 1))]
330	    K = len(primes)
331	
332	    S = prover_tables(n, primes)
333	    if corrupt_layer is not None:
334	        i = corrupt_layer
335	        S[i] = S[i].copy()
336	        S[i][x] += 1  # off-by-one in the DP table at the output value
337	        v = np.arange(1 << n, dtype=np.int64)
338	        for j in range(i + 1, K + 1):
339	            p = primes[j - 1]
340	            b = v >= p * p
341	            S[j] = S[j - 1] - b * (S[j - 1][v // p] - (j - 1))
342	
343	    claimed_pi = int(S[K][x])
344	    Sfield = [(s % Q).astype(np.uint64) for s in S]
345	
346	    stats = {"t_prover": 0.0, "t_verifier": 0.0, "comm": 0}
347	    z = [(x >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]  # Boolean output point
348	    claim = claimed_pi % Q
349	    for i in range(K, 0, -1):
350	        ok, z, claim = verify_layer(i, primes[i - 1], n, z, claim,
351	                                    Sfield[i - 1], rng, stats, patch=patch)
352	        if not ok:
353	            return dict(accepted=False, claimed=claimed_pi, layers=K,
354	                        **stats)
355	    # base layer: closed form, O(n)
356	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
357	    ok = s0_closed_form(z) == claim % Q
358	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
359	    return dict(accepted=ok, claimed=claimed_pi, layers=K, **stats)
360	
361	
362	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
363	# tests / experiments
364	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
365	
366	def direct_pi(x):
367	    sieve = np.ones(x + 1, dtype=bool)
368	    sieve[:2] = False
369	    for p in range(2, int(x ** 0.5) + 1):
370	        if sieve[p]:
371	            sieve[p * p::p] = False
372	    return int(sieve.sum())
373	
374	
375	def selftest():
376	    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
377	    n = 8
378	    # W automaton vs floor division on Boolean points
379	    for p in (2, 3, 7, 13):
380	        for _ in range(200):
381	            v = int(rng.integers(0, 1 << n))
382	            u = int(rng.integers(0, 1 << n))
383	            bv = [(v >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
384	            bu = [(u >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
385	            assert w_div_eval(bv, bu, p, n) == (1 if u == v // p else 0)
386	    # comparator vs >=
387	    for M in (0, 1, 37, 200, 255):
388	        for v in range(1 << n):
389	            bv = [(v >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
390	            assert ge_const_eval(bv, M, n) == (1 if v >= M else 0)
391	    # S0 closed form vs table MLE at random field points
392	    v = np.arange(1 << n, dtype=np.int64)
393	    S0 = (np.maximum(v - 1, 0) % Q).astype(np.uint64)
394	    for _ in range(20):
395	        pt = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(n)]
396	        assert s0_closed_form(pt) == mle_eval(S0, pt)
397	    # single-layer reduction consistency at random z
398	    primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13]
399	    S = prover_tables(n, primes)
400	    Sf = [(s % Q).astype(np.uint64) for s in S]
401	    i, p = 4, primes[3]
402	    pt = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(n)]
403	    claim = mle_eval(Sf[i], pt)
404	    stats = {"t_prover": 0, "t_verifier": 0, "comm": 0}
405	    ok, z2, c2 = verify_layer(i, p, n, pt, claim, Sf[i - 1],
406	                              np.random.default_rng(1), stats)
407	    assert ok and c2 == mle_eval(Sf[i - 1], z2)
408	    # tiny end-to-end
409	    res = run_protocol(10, np.random.default_rng(2))
410	    assert res["accepted"] and res["claimed"] == direct_pi((1 << 10) - 1)
411	    print("selftest OK")
412	
413	
414	def main(n, cheat_trials, seed):
415	    x = (1 << n) - 1
416	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
417	
418	    res = run_protocol(n, rng)
419	    truth = direct_pi(x)
420	    print(f"x = 2^{n}-1 = {x}, layers (primes <= sqrt x): {res['layers']}")
421	    print(f"honest run: {'ACCEPTED' if res['accepted'] else 'REJECTED'}, "
422	          f"claimed pi(x) = {res['claimed']}, direct sieve pi(x) = {truth}, "
423	          f"match = {res['claimed'] == truth}")
424	    assert res["accepted"] and res["claimed"] == truth
425	    print(f"t_prover = {res['t_prover']:.2f}s   "
426	          f"t_verifier = {res['t_verifier']*1000:.1f}ms   "
427	          f"communication = {res['comm']} field elems "
428	          f"(~{res['comm']*4/1024:.1f} KB)")
429	
430	    rej_patch = 0
431	    for t in range(cheat_trials):
432	        r = run_protocol(n, np.random.default_rng(seed + 100 + t),
433	                         patch=True, corrupt_layer=res["layers"] // 2)
434	        rej_patch += (not r["accepted"])
435	    print(f"self-consistent liar + adaptive round patching: "
436	          f"rejected {rej_patch}/{cheat_trials}")
437	
438	    rej_cor = 0
439	    for t in range(cheat_trials):
440	        r = run_protocol(n, np.random.default_rng(seed + 500 + t),
441	                         corrupt_layer=res["layers"] // 2)
442	        rej_cor += (not r["accepted"])
443	    print(f"self-consistent liar (honest protocol on corrupted DP): "
444	          f"rejected {rej_cor}/{cheat_trials}")
445	    nK = n * res["layers"]
446	    print(f"soundness bound ~ 7nK/q = {7*nK/Q:.2e}")
447	
448	
449	if __name__ == "__main__":
450	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
451	    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=16)
452	    ap.add_argument("--cheat-trials", type=int, default=25)
453	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
454	    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
455	    args = ap.parse_args()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
lucy_dp_verification.py — interactive proof for the EXACT value of pi(x).

An untrusted prover runs the Lucy_Hedgehog / Legendre sieve DP and then
convinces a verifier of the exact value of pi(x) with UNCONDITIONAL
(information-theoretic) soundness. The verifier checks every layer of
the DP recursion via sum-check without ever sieving, touching only
O(n)-size objects per layer plus an O(n*p) automaton evaluation for the
floor-division wiring.

Protocol (new object, S491). State function after sieving by the first
i primes, defined for ALL v in [0, 2^n):

    S_0(v) = max(v - 1, 0)                       (count of 2..v)
    S_i(v) = S_{i-1}(v) - b_i(v) * (S_{i-1}(floor(v/p_i)) - (i-1))

where b_i(v) = [v >= p_i^2]. The recurrence holds pointwise for every v
(Lucy_Hedgehog), and S_K(x) = pi(x) once K = pi(sqrt(x)). Crucially
S_{i-1}(p_i - 1) = i - 1 is a PUBLIC constant (the primes below p_i),
so each layer's correction scalar needs no extra claim.

Per layer i (claim: tilde{S_i}(z) = C):
  Phase A  (n rounds, degree <= 3): sum-check of
      C = sum_v eq(z,v) * [ S(v) - B(v) * (G(v) - (i-1)) ]
    with G(v) := S_{i-1}(floor(v/p_i)) as an independent table; ends
    with prover claims s1 = tilde{S}(r_v), g1 = tilde{G}(r_v); verifier
    evaluates eq(z, r_v) in O(n) and tilde{B}(r_v) by a 3-state
    comparator automaton in O(n), and checks the combination.
  Phase B  (n rounds, degree <= 2): sum-check of
      g1 = sum_u W(r_v, u) * S(u),   W(v,u) = [u = floor(v/p_i)]
    ends with claim s2 = tilde{S}(r_u); verifier evaluates
    tilde{W}(r_v, r_u) by the LONG-DIVISION AUTOMATON: p states
    (the running remainder), reading bits of v MSB-first and emitting
    the quotient bits of u — O(n*p) per layer. This is the structured-
    wiring primitive that makes the verifier sublinear.
  Line batching: the two claims s1@r_v, s2@r_u about tilde{S_{i-1}}
    reduce to one claim at a random point on the line through them
    (prover sends the degree-<=n restriction).
Base layer: tilde{S_0}(z) = Int(z) - 1 + prod_j (1 - z_j), a closed
form the verifier evaluates in O(n). Int(z) = sum_j 2^{n-1-j} z_j.

Costs: prover O~(K * 2^n) here (table-based demo; a production prover
works on the O(sqrt x)-size compressed Lucy table). Verifier
O(n * sum_{p <= sqrt x} p) field ops with the automaton wiring;
communication O(K * n) field elements. Soundness error <= ~7nK/q,
unconditional. Field q = 2^31 - 1 for numpy-exact arithmetic (a
production protocol lifts to q ~ 2^61 or an extension field).

What would falsify this construction: an accepted honest run whose
output differs from a direct sieve's pi(x); a cheating prover (wrong
claim, adaptive round patching, or a corrupted DP table propagated
consistently downstream) accepted at a rate above the soundness bound;
or verifier work scaling with 2^n instead of n * sum p.

Usage:
  python3 lucy_dp_verification.py --selftest
  python3 lucy_dp_verification.py --n 16 --cheat-trials 25
"""

import argparse
import time

import numpy as np

Q = (1 << 31) - 1


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# small field helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def lagrange_eval(ys, r):
    """Evaluate the polynomial through (j, ys[j]), j = 0..deg, at r."""
    k = len(ys) - 1
    r = int(r) % Q
    total = 0
    for i in range(k + 1):
        num, den = 1, 1
        for j in range(k + 1):
            if j == i:
                continue
            num = (num * ((r - j) % Q)) % Q
            den = (den * ((i - j) % Q)) % Q
        total = (total + ys[i] * num % Q * pow(den, Q - 2, Q)) % Q
    return total


def eq_table(z):
    """Table of eq~(z, w) over Boolean w; index bit j (MSB-first) pairs
    with z[j]. PROVER-side object: O(2^n)."""
    t = np.array([1], dtype=np.uint64)
    for zj in reversed([int(v) % Q for v in z]):
        a = (t * ((Q + 1 - zj) % Q)) % Q
        b = (t * zj) % Q
        t = np.concatenate([a, b])
    return t


def eq_point(a, b):
    """eq~(a, b) for two field points. VERIFIER: O(n)."""
    acc = 1
    for x, y in zip(a, b):
        x, y = int(x) % Q, int(y) % Q
        acc = acc * ((x * y + (Q + 1 - x) * (Q + 1 - y)) % Q) % Q
    return acc


def mle_eval(table, pt):
    """tilde{table}(pt). PROVER-side: O(2^n)."""
    return int((table * eq_table(pt) % Q).sum(dtype=np.uint64) % Q)


def int_of_point(z):
    """Int(z) = sum_j 2^{n-1-j} z_j mod Q (degree-1 extension of the
    bits-to-integer map)."""
    n = len(z)
    return sum((1 << (n - 1 - j)) % Q * (int(z[j]) % Q) for j in range(n)) % Q


def s0_closed_form(z):
    """tilde{S_0}(z) = Int(z) - 1 + prod_j(1 - z_j). VERIFIER: O(n)."""
    prod = 1
    for zj in z:
        prod = prod * ((Q + 1 - int(zj)) % Q) % Q
    return (int_of_point(z) - 1 + prod) % Q


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# verifier-side automaton evaluations (the structured-wiring primitives)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def ge_const_eval(rv, M, n):
    """MLE of [v >= M] at point rv. 3-state comparator (equal-so-far /
    greater / less), bits MSB-first. VERIFIER: O(n)."""
    st = [1, 0, 0]
    for j in range(n):
        mj = (M >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1
        w = [(Q + 1 - int(rv[j])) % Q, int(rv[j]) % Q]
        new = [0, 0, 0]
        for a in (0, 1):
            if a == mj:
                new[0] += st[0] * w[a]
            elif a > mj:
                new[1] += st[0] * w[a]
            else:
                new[2] += st[0] * w[a]
            new[1] += st[1] * w[a]
            new[2] += st[2] * w[a]
        st = [x % Q for x in new]
    return (st[0] + st[1]) % Q


def w_div_eval(rv, ru, p, n):
    """MLE of W(v, u) = [u = floor(v/p)] at (rv, ru). Long-division
    automaton: state = running remainder (< p); reading bit a of v
    MSB-first from state s gives t = 2s + a, emits quotient bit
    floor(t/p) and moves to t mod p. VERIFIER: O(n*p)."""
    st = [0] * p
    st[0] = 1
    for j in range(n):
        wv = [(Q + 1 - int(rv[j])) % Q, int(rv[j]) % Q]
        wu = [(Q + 1 - int(ru[j])) % Q, int(ru[j]) % Q]
        new = [0] * p
        for s in range(p):
            if st[s] == 0:
                continue
            for a in (0, 1):
                t = 2 * s + a
                b, s2 = divmod(t, p)
                new[s2] = (new[s2] + st[s] * wv[a] % Q * wu[b]) % Q
        st = new
    return sum(st) % Q


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# generic sum-check over products of multilinear tables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def sumcheck(claim, tables, terms, degree, rng, patch=False):
    """Sum-check for  claim = sum_w  sum_terms coef * prod tables[name][w].
    tables: dict name -> uint64 array (consumed). Interleaved prover
    (round polynomials by table halving) and verifier (consistency
    checks, random challenges). patch=True simulates an adaptive
    cheating prover that fixes up g(0) each round to mask a false claim.
    Returns (ok, r_list, final_claim, bound_scalars)."""
    nvars = int(np.log2(len(next(iter(tables.values())))))
    rs = []
    c = int(claim) % Q
    for _ in range(nvars):
        evals = []
        for X in range(degree + 1):
            xf = X % Q
            xc = (Q + 1 - X) % Q
            tot = 0
            for coef, names in terms:
                prod = None
                for nm in names:
                    tb = tables[nm]
                    h = len(tb) >> 1
                    row = (tb[:h] * xc + tb[h:] * xf) % Q
                    prod = row if prod is None else (prod * row) % Q
                tot = (tot + (coef % Q) * int(prod.sum(dtype=np.uint64) % Q)) % Q
            evals.append(tot)
        if patch:
            deficit = (c - (evals[0] + evals[1])) % Q
            evals[0] = (evals[0] + deficit) % Q
        # verifier checks and challenges
        if (evals[0] + evals[1]) % Q != c:
            return False, rs, None, None
        r = int(rng.integers(0, Q))
        rs.append(r)
        c = lagrange_eval(evals, r)
        # bind the variable in all tables
        rc = (Q + 1 - r) % Q
        for nm in tables:
            tb = tables[nm]
            h = len(tb) >> 1
            tables[nm] = (tb[:h] * rc + tb[h:] * r) % Q
    scalars = {nm: int(tables[nm][0]) for nm in tables}
    return True, rs, c, scalars


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the layered protocol
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def prover_tables(n, primes):
    """Prover precomputes all DP layers S_0..S_K (exact integers)."""
    N = 1 << n
    v = np.arange(N, dtype=np.int64)
    S = [np.maximum(v - 1, 0)]
    for i, p in enumerate(primes, start=1):
        prev = S[-1]
        b = v >= p * p
        upd = prev - b * (prev[v // p] - (i - 1))
        S.append(upd)
    return S


def verify_layer(i, p, n, z, claim, S_prev_field, rng, stats,
                 patch=False):
    """One layer reduction: claim about tilde{S_i}(z) -> claim about
    tilde{S_{i-1}} at a single new point. Returns (ok, new_z, new_claim)."""
    N = 1 << n
    v = np.arange(N, dtype=np.int64)
    c_i = (i - 1) % Q

    # ---- prover builds phase-A tables (O(2^n)) ----
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    EQ = eq_table(z)
    Sf = S_prev_field.copy()
    Bf = (v >= p * p).astype(np.uint64)
    Gf = S_prev_field[v // p]
    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0

    termsA = [(1, ["EQ", "S"]), (Q - 1, ["EQ", "B", "G"]),
              (c_i, ["EQ", "B"])]
    okA, r_v, finalA, scal = sumcheck(claim, {"EQ": EQ, "S": Sf, "B": Bf,
                                              "G": Gf}, termsA, 3, rng,
                                      patch=patch)
    if not okA:
        return False, None, None
    s1, g1 = scal["S"], scal["G"]  # prover claims

    # ---- verifier-side phase-A final check (O(n)) ----
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    eqv = eq_point(z, r_v)
    bv = ge_const_eval(r_v, p * p, n)
    expect = eqv * ((s1 - bv * ((g1 - c_i) % Q)) % Q) % Q
    ok = (finalA % Q) == expect
    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
    if not ok:
        return False, None, None

    # ---- phase B: verify g1 against the division wiring ----
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    Wt = np.zeros(N, dtype=np.uint64)
    np.add.at(Wt, v // p, eq_table(r_v))   # sums of < p terms < Q each
    Wt %= Q
    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0

    okB, r_u, finalB, scalB = sumcheck(g1, {"W": Wt,
                                            "S": S_prev_field.copy()},
                                       [(1, ["W", "S"])], 2, rng,
                                       patch=patch)
    if not okB:
        return False, None, None
    s2 = scalB["S"]

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    wv = w_div_eval(r_v, r_u, p, n)
    ok = (finalB % Q) == wv * s2 % Q
    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
    if not ok:
        return False, None, None

    # ---- line batching: s1@r_v, s2@r_u -> one claim ----
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    line_pts = []
    for t in range(n + 1):
        tf = t % Q
        gpt = [((Q + 1 - tf) * int(a) + tf * int(b)) % Q
               for a, b in zip(r_v, r_u)]
        line_pts.append(gpt)
    hs = [mle_eval(S_prev_field, gp) for gp in line_pts]  # prover
    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    if hs[0] != s1 or hs[1] != s2:   # verifier checks endpoints
        stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
        return False, None, None
    tstar = int(rng.integers(0, Q))
    new_claim = lagrange_eval(hs, tstar)
    tf = tstar % Q
    new_z = [((Q + 1 - tf) * int(a) + tf * int(b)) % Q
             for a, b in zip(r_v, r_u)]
    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
    stats["comm"] += (4 * n) + (3 * n) + (n + 1) + 2  # field elems sent
    return True, new_z, new_claim


def run_protocol(n, rng, patch=False, corrupt_layer=None):
    """Full chain: verify pi(2^n - 1). Returns dict with outcome.
    corrupt_layer=i: prover corrupts one entry of S_i and recomputes
    all later layers consistently (a 'self-consistent liar')."""
    x = (1 << n) - 1
    primes = [p for p in range(2, int(x ** 0.5) + 1)
              if all(p % d for d in range(2, int(p ** 0.5) + 1))]
    K = len(primes)

    S = prover_tables(n, primes)
    if corrupt_layer is not None:
        i = corrupt_layer
        S[i] = S[i].copy()
        S[i][x] += 1  # off-by-one in the DP table at the output value
        v = np.arange(1 << n, dtype=np.int64)
        for j in range(i + 1, K + 1):
            p = primes[j - 1]
            b = v >= p * p
            S[j] = S[j - 1] - b * (S[j - 1][v // p] - (j - 1))

    claimed_pi = int(S[K][x])
    Sfield = [(s % Q).astype(np.uint64) for s in S]

    stats = {"t_prover": 0.0, "t_verifier": 0.0, "comm": 0}
    z = [(x >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]  # Boolean output point
    claim = claimed_pi % Q
    for i in range(K, 0, -1):
        ok, z, claim = verify_layer(i, primes[i - 1], n, z, claim,
                                    Sfield[i - 1], rng, stats, patch=patch)
        if not ok:
            return dict(accepted=False, claimed=claimed_pi, layers=K,
                        **stats)
    # base layer: closed form, O(n)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    ok = s0_closed_form(z) == claim % Q
    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
    return dict(accepted=ok, claimed=claimed_pi, layers=K, **stats)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests / experiments
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def direct_pi(x):
    sieve = np.ones(x + 1, dtype=bool)
    sieve[:2] = False
    for p in range(2, int(x ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p * p::p] = False
    return int(sieve.sum())


def selftest():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    n = 8
    # W automaton vs floor division on Boolean points
    for p in (2, 3, 7, 13):
        for _ in range(200):
            v = int(rng.integers(0, 1 << n))
            u = int(rng.integers(0, 1 << n))
            bv = [(v >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
            bu = [(u >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
            assert w_div_eval(bv, bu, p, n) == (1 if u == v // p else 0)
    # comparator vs >=
    for M in (0, 1, 37, 200, 255):
        for v in range(1 << n):
            bv = [(v >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)]
            assert ge_const_eval(bv, M, n) == (1 if v >= M else 0)
    # S0 closed form vs table MLE at random field points
    v = np.arange(1 << n, dtype=np.int64)
    S0 = (np.maximum(v - 1, 0) % Q).astype(np.uint64)
    for _ in range(20):
        pt = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(n)]
        assert s0_closed_form(pt) == mle_eval(S0, pt)
    # single-layer reduction consistency at random z
    primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13]
    S = prover_tables(n, primes)
    Sf = [(s % Q).astype(np.uint64) for s in S]
    i, p = 4, primes[3]
    pt = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(n)]
    claim = mle_eval(Sf[i], pt)
    stats = {"t_prover": 0, "t_verifier": 0, "comm": 0}
    ok, z2, c2 = verify_layer(i, p, n, pt, claim, Sf[i - 1],
                              np.random.default_rng(1), stats)
    assert ok and c2 == mle_eval(Sf[i - 1], z2)
    # tiny end-to-end
    res = run_protocol(10, np.random.default_rng(2))
    assert res["accepted"] and res["claimed"] == direct_pi((1 << 10) - 1)
    print("selftest OK")


def main(n, cheat_trials, seed):
    x = (1 << n) - 1
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    res = run_protocol(n, rng)
    truth = direct_pi(x)
    print(f"x = 2^{n}-1 = {x}, layers (primes <= sqrt x): {res['layers']}")
    print(f"honest run: {'ACCEPTED' if res['accepted'] else 'REJECTED'}, "
          f"claimed pi(x) = {res['claimed']}, direct sieve pi(x) = {truth}, "
          f"match = {res['claimed'] == truth}")
    assert res["accepted"] and res["claimed"] == truth
    print(f"t_prover = {res['t_prover']:.2f}s   "
          f"t_verifier = {res['t_verifier']*1000:.1f}ms   "
          f"communication = {res['comm']} field elems "
          f"(~{res['comm']*4/1024:.1f} KB)")

    rej_patch = 0
    for t in range(cheat_trials):
        r = run_protocol(n, np.random.default_rng(seed + 100 + t),
                         patch=True, corrupt_layer=res["layers"] // 2)
        rej_patch += (not r["accepted"])
    print(f"self-consistent liar + adaptive round patching: "
          f"rejected {rej_patch}/{cheat_trials}")

    rej_cor = 0
    for t in range(cheat_trials):
        r = run_protocol(n, np.random.default_rng(seed + 500 + t),
                         corrupt_layer=res["layers"] // 2)
        rej_cor += (not r["accepted"])
    print(f"self-consistent liar (honest protocol on corrupted DP): "
          f"rejected {rej_cor}/{cheat_trials}")
    nK = n * res["layers"]
    print(f"soundness bound ~ 7nK/q = {7*nK/Q:.2e}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--cheat-trials", type=int, default=25)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.selftest:
        selftest()
    else:
        main(args.n, args.cheat_trials, args.seed)

6	lucy_dp_delegated_wiring.py) has an Õ(sqrt x) VERIFIER but an Õ(x^{3/2})
7	table-based demo PROVER, because the demo materializes every DP layer over
8	the full 2^n value space. A production prover must work the O(sqrt x)-size
9	compressed Lucy state: the small side (values v <= sqrt x, value-addressed)
10	and the large side (values floor(x/d), d-addressed by the index d).
11	
12	The large-side layer update needs S_{i-1}(floor(floor(x/d)/p)) =
13	S_{i-1}(floor(x/(d p))). When d p <= sqrt x this is large-side index d p
14	(multiply the INDEX by the constant p -> affine wiring, existing
15	machinery). When d p > sqrt x the target floor(x/(d p)) is a SMALL value
16	and must be looked up by value in the small side -- which requires the
17	verifier to be convinced of floor(x/(d p)) WITHOUT computing it. That is a
18	division of the public constant x by the prover-variable (d p): the
19	certifying identity
20	
21	        u_d * (d p) + r_d = x ,   0 <= r_d < d p
22	
23	has the product u_d * d of two quantities that BOTH range over the batch
24	(p fixed within a layer), i.e. a genuine variable x variable
25	multiplication. This script builds and tests, in isolation, the batched
26	sum-check primitive that certifies a claim of the form
27	
28	        C = sum_{d in {0,1}^m}  eq(rho, d) * S~( u_d ) ,
29	        u_d = floor( X / a_d ),   a_d = (dstart + d) * p ,
30	
31	where S is the (committed) small-side table, rho a verifier point, and the
32	correctness of every u_d is enforced ENTIRELY by prover-supplied trace
33	tables checked through low-degree multilinear identities. The verifier
34	never divides and never touches a quotient.
35	
36	Construction (all over the d-cube of size D = 2^m unless noted):
37	  Witness tables: U[d]=u_d, R[d]=r_d, Qv[d]=q_d=a_d-1-r_d, the MSB-first
38	  bit decompositions Ub_j (Lv bits of u_d), Rb_j / Qb_j (Lr bits of r_d /
39	  q_d), the wiring table A[d]=a_d, and ONE[d]=1.
40	  Constraint zero-test (one degree-3 sum-check at a random point tau,
41	  constraints batched by powers of a random alpha):
42	    * bitness        T*(1-T)=0           for every bit table
43	    * recomposition  U = sum 2^j Ub_j , R = sum 2^j Rb_j , Qv = sum 2^j Qb_j
44	    * multiply+rem   U*a_d + R - X = 0      (a_d via the verifier's own
45	                                             degree-1 wiring a~(pt)=p*(e+dstart))
46	    * remainder bnd  a_d - 1 - R - Qv = 0   (q_d>=0, a sum of bits, => r_d<a_d)
47	  Together with the bit-ranges these pin u_d = floor(X/a_d) UNIQUELY.
48	  Lookup (the claim C): route C = sum_v S(v)*omega(v) with
49	  omega(v)=sum_d eq(rho,d)[u_d=v]; verify by two sum-checks --
50	    B1 (deg 2, v-cube): C = sum_v S~(v) omega~(v) -> claims S~(r_B), omega~(r_B);
51	    B2 (deg Lv+1, d-cube): omega~(r_B) = sum_d eq(rho,d) prod_j EB_j(d),
52	       EB_j(d) = eq(r_B[j], Ub_j(d)) the per-bit selector built from the
53	       SAME committed Ub_j proven above.
54	
55	THE FIELD LIFT (S498). The soundness of the multiply identity U*a+R-X=0
56	depends on |F| being a TRUE upper bound on the integers it relates. The
57	demo prime q = 2^31-1 is sound only while every certified integer (values,
58	and the product U*a ~ X) stays below q, i.e. n <~ 30. Above that a cheating
59	prover can supply a *different* Lv-bit quotient U'' and remainder R'' < a
60	with U''*a + R'' = X + k*q for some k >= 1: this aliases to X mod q (so the
61	field check passes) yet U'' != floor(X/a). The bit-range tables alone do
62	NOT stop it -- U'' = floor((X+kq)/a) is a genuine Lv-bit integer whenever
63	2^Lv has headroom (precisely the regime q < X). This is a real soundness
64	hole of the demo above its field, not a stylistic caveat.
65	
66	  *** The fix is to RAISE THE CHARACTERISTIC: a prime field F_Q with
67	      prime Q > (the largest integer the identity relates). ***
68	
69	  q = 2^31-1   characteristic 2^31-1, sound for n <~ 30
70	  Q = 2^61-1   characteristic 2^61-1, sound for n <~ 60 (Mersenne, mulmod
71	               needs >64-bit intermediates -> Python-int object arrays here)

73	  A NON-FIX, recorded so it is not retried: the EXTENSION field F_{q^2}.
74	  |F_{q^2}| = q^2 ~ 2^62 counts the number of ELEMENTS, but its
75	  CHARACTERISTIC is still q. Integers embed mod the characteristic, so an
76	  integer k*q embeds as the degree-0 element (k*q mod q, 0) = (0,0) = the
77	  ZERO of F_{q^2}. The wrap-around forgery differs from the truth by
78	  exactly k*q, hence is the SAME element of F_{q^2} as the truth -- F_{q^2}
79	  cannot tell them apart no matter how the challenges are drawn (the larger
80	  element count only shrinks the Schwartz-Zippel error, an orthogonal
81	  concern). `--refute-q2` demonstrates this directly. The genuine
82	  alternative to a larger prime is a small-field schoolbook CARRY trace
83	  (limb products + carry constraints), which never asks the field to hold
84	  the product; that is a separate construction, not a field swap.
85	
86	This file therefore runs the primitive over an arbitrary prime modulus
87	(--field q | big | small, or --qmod). The sum-check skeleton, the trace
88	identities and the cost accounting (verifier polylog, prover Õ(√x)) are all
89	field-agnostic; only the modulus and the numpy dtype (uint64 vs object for
90	>32-bit primes) change.

92	Leaf claims about committed witness tables (U, R, bits, S, omega at the
93	final sum-check points) are closed in this ISOLATED harness by direct MLE
94	evaluation -- the stand-in for the polynomial-commitment opening / outer-
95	protocol line-batching that integration supplies.

98	quotient, wrong remainder, non-Boolean bit, corrupted lookup table, wrong
99	claimed C, OR a wrap-around alias) accepted by a field whose characteristic
100	exceeds the integers in play; or the verifier work scaling with D = 2^m or
101	with a quotient size instead of with m and Lv.
102	
103	Usage:
104	  python3 compressed_prover_mult_trace.py --selftest
105	  python3 compressed_prover_mult_trace.py --n 12 --p 7 --field q
106	  python3 compressed_prover_mult_trace.py --n 34 --p 7 --field big --alias-demo
107	  python3 compressed_prover_mult_trace.py --refute-q2
108	  python3 compressed_prover_mult_trace.py --bench

128	    """numpy dtype: uint64 keeps a+b of two products below 2^64 only while
129	    q <= 2^31-1; larger primes fall back to exact Python-int objects."""
130	    return np.uint64 if q <= DEFAULT_Q else object

135	    if arr.dtype == object:

137	    return int(arr.sum(dtype=np.uint64) % q)

140	def lagrange_eval(ys, r, q):
141	    """Evaluate the polynomial through (j, ys[j]), j=0..deg, at r over F_q."""
142	    k = len(ys) - 1
143	    r = int(r) % q
144	    total = 0
145	    for i in range(k + 1):
146	        num, den = 1, 1
147	        for j in range(k + 1):
148	            if j == i:
149	                continue
150	            num = (num * ((r - j) % q)) % q
151	            den = (den * ((i - j) % q)) % q
152	        total = (total + int(ys[i]) * num % q * pow(den, q - 2, q)) % q
153	    return total

158	    t = np.array([1], dtype=_dt(q))
159	    for zj in reversed([int(v) % q for v in z]):
160	        a = (t * ((q + 1 - zj) % q)) % q
161	        b = (t * zj) % q
162	        t = np.concatenate([a, b])

168	    acc = 1
169	    for x, y in zip(a, b):

171	        acc = acc * ((x * y + (q + 1 - x) * (q + 1 - y)) % q) % q

176	    """tilde{table}(pt). PROVER-side: O(2^n)."""
177	    return _asum((table * eq_table(pt, q)) % q, q)

182	    n = len(z)
183	    return sum((1 << (n - 1 - j)) % q * (int(z[j]) % q) for j in range(n)) % q

185	
186	def sumcheck(claim, tables, terms, degree, rng, q):
187	    """Sum-check for claim = sum_w sum_terms coef * prod tables[name][w] over
188	    F_q. tables: dict name -> field array (consumed). Returns
189	    (ok, r_list, final_claim, bound_scalars). Field-agnostic: the dtype of
190	    the input tables (uint64 or object) carries the modulus size."""
191	    nvars = int(round(np.log2(len(next(iter(tables.values()))))))
192	    rs = []
193	    c = int(claim) % q
194	    for _ in range(nvars):
195	        evals = []
196	        for X in range(degree + 1):
197	            xf = X % q
198	            xc = (q + 1 - X) % q
199	            tot = 0
200	            for coef, names in terms:
201	                prod = None
202	                for nm in names:
203	                    tb = tables[nm]
204	                    h = len(tb) >> 1
205	                    row = (tb[:h] * xc + tb[h:] * xf) % q
206	                    prod = row if prod is None else (prod * row) % q
207	                tot = (tot + (coef % q) * _asum(prod, q)) % q
208	            evals.append(tot)
209	        if (evals[0] + evals[1]) % q != c:
210	            return False, rs, None, None
211	        r = int(rng.integers(0, q))
212	        rs.append(r)
213	        c = lagrange_eval(evals, r, q)
214	        rc = (q + 1 - r) % q
215	        for nm in list(tables):
216	            tb = tables[nm]
217	            h = len(tb) >> 1
218	            tables[nm] = (tb[:h] * rc + tb[h:] * r) % q
219	    scalars = {nm: int(tables[nm][0]) for nm in tables}
220	    return True, rs, c, scalars

228	    """MLE of a_e = (dstart + e)*p at a field point pt (e = Int(pt)). O(m)."""

233	# honest prover: the compressed trace over the d-cube
234	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
235	
236	def build_witness(X, p, m, dstart, q=DEFAULT_Q):
237	    """Materialize the trace tables for a_e = (dstart+e)*p, e in [0, 2^m).
238	    Integer arrays (u, r, q-complement, a) are kept so the witness can be
239	    re-materialised over a different prime (`rematerialize`) or forged
240	    (`forge_alias`)."""
241	    D = 1 << m
242	    e = np.arange(D, dtype=np.int64)
243	    a = (e + dstart) * p
244	    u = X // a
245	    r = X - u * a
246	    qd = a - 1 - r
247	    assert (r >= 0).all() and (r < a).all() and (qd >= 0).all()
248	    Lv = max(int(u.max()).bit_length(), 1)
249	    Lr = max(int(a.max()).bit_length(), 1)
250	    W = dict(D=D, m=m, Lv=Lv, Lr=Lr, u=u, r=r, q=qd, a=a, p=p,
251	             dstart=dstart, X=X, mod=q)
252	    _materialize(W, q)
253	    return W

256	def _materialize(W, q):
257	    """(Re)build the field tables of W over modulus q from its integer
258	    arrays. Bit tables are 0/1 (field-independent); U/R/Qv/A reduce mod q."""
259	    dt = _dt(q)
260	    u, r, qd, a = W["u"], W["r"], W["q"], W["a"]
261	    D, Lv, Lr = W["D"], W["Lv"], W["Lr"]
262	    tabs = {
263	        "U": (u % q).astype(dt),
264	        "R": (r % q).astype(dt),
265	        "Qv": (qd % q).astype(dt),
266	        "A": (a % q).astype(dt),
267	        "ONE": np.ones(D, dtype=dt),
268	    }
269	    for j in range(Lv):
270	        tabs[f"Ub{j}"] = ((u >> (Lv - 1 - j)) & 1).astype(dt)
271	    for j in range(Lr):
272	        tabs[f"Rb{j}"] = ((r >> (Lr - 1 - j)) & 1).astype(dt)
273	        tabs[f"Qb{j}"] = ((qd >> (Lr - 1 - j)) & 1).astype(dt)
274	    W["tabs"] = tabs
275	    W["mod"] = q
276	    return W
277	
278	
279	def rematerialize(W, q):
280	    """Switch a (possibly forged) witness to a different prime field."""
281	    return _materialize(W, q)

284	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
285	# wrap-around alias forgery (the soundness hole the field lift closes)
286	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
287	
288	def forge_alias(W, alias_mod):
289	    """Return (W2, info): a copy of W with ONE entry's quotient replaced by a
290	    wrap-around alias u'' = floor((X + k*alias_mod)/a) that satisfies
291	    u''*a + r'' = X + k*alias_mod with u'' an Lv-bit integer and 0<=r''<a.
292	    Hence u''*a + r'' == X (mod alias_mod) but != X over the integers (and
293	    != X mod any prime > X + k*alias_mod). Searches entries with the most
294	    Lv-headroom (largest a -> smallest u) first, k>=1 up to 64. Returns
295	    (None, None) when no alias fits (e.g. alias_mod > X, the safe regime).
296	    W2 carries forged INTEGER arrays; call rematerialize(W2, test_q) before
297	    verifying over a chosen field."""
298	    X, Lv = W["X"], W["Lv"]
299	    cap = 1 << Lv
300	    a_arr, u_arr = W["a"], W["u"]
301	    for e0 in np.argsort(-a_arr):          # large a first => most headroom
302	        a = int(a_arr[e0])
303	        u_true = int(u_arr[e0])
304	        for k in range(1, 65):
305	            num = X + k * alias_mod
306	            upp = num // a
307	            rpp = num - upp * a
308	            if upp != u_true and upp < cap and 0 <= rpp < a:
309	                W2 = dict(W)
310	                W2["u"] = W["u"].copy()
311	                W2["r"] = W["r"].copy()
312	                W2["q"] = W["q"].copy()
313	                W2["u"][e0] = upp
314	                W2["r"][e0] = rpp
315	                W2["q"][e0] = a - 1 - rpp
316	                return W2, dict(e0=int(e0), k=int(k), a=a, u_true=u_true,
317	                                u_forged=int(upp), r_forged=int(rpp))
318	    return None, None

322	# the batched constraint zero-test (degree-3 sum-check)
323	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
324	
325	def build_terms(Lv, Lr, X, alpha, q):
326	    """Flat (coef,[names]) term list for F = sum_c alpha^c * constraint_c,
327	    every term carrying the eq-selector EQ. Order MUST match
328	    constraint_eval below (selftest checks honest equivalence)."""
329	    ap = [pow(int(alpha), k, q) for k in range(6 + Lv + 2 * Lr)]
330	    negX = (q - (X % q)) % q
331	    terms = []
332	    a1 = ap[1]                                              # c1: U*a + R - X
333	    terms += [(a1, ["EQ", "U", "A"]), (a1, ["EQ", "R"]),
334	              (a1 * negX % q, ["EQ", "ONE"])]
335	    a2 = ap[2]                                              # c2: a - 1 - R - Qv
336	    terms += [(a2, ["EQ", "A"]), ((q - a2) % q, ["EQ", "ONE"]),
337	              ((q - a2) % q, ["EQ", "R"]), ((q - a2) % q, ["EQ", "Qv"])]
338	    a3 = ap[3]                                              # c3: recompU
339	    terms.append((a3, ["EQ", "U"]))
340	    for j in range(Lv):
341	        terms.append(((q - a3 * pow(2, Lv - 1 - j, q)) % q, ["EQ", f"Ub{j}"]))
342	    a4 = ap[4]                                              # c4: recompR
343	    terms.append((a4, ["EQ", "R"]))
344	    for j in range(Lr):
345	        terms.append(((q - a4 * pow(2, Lr - 1 - j, q)) % q, ["EQ", f"Rb{j}"]))
346	    a5 = ap[5]                                              # c5: recompQ
347	    terms.append((a5, ["EQ", "Qv"]))
348	    for j in range(Lr):
349	        terms.append(((q - a5 * pow(2, Lr - 1 - j, q)) % q, ["EQ", f"Qb{j}"]))
350	    c = 6                                                   # c6..: bitness
351	    for nm in ([f"Ub{j}" for j in range(Lv)]
352	               + [f"Rb{j}" for j in range(Lr)]
353	               + [f"Qb{j}" for j in range(Lr)]):
354	        ac = ap[c]
355	        c += 1
356	        terms += [(ac, ["EQ", nm]), ((q - ac) % q, ["EQ", nm, nm])]
357	    return terms
358	
359	
360	def constraint_eval(scal, av, X, Lv, Lr, alpha, q):
361	    """Verifier's recomputation of F/eq at the final point from the bound
362	    witness scalars (U,R,Qv,bits) and its OWN wiring value av = a~(r). The
363	    prover's EQ/A/ONE scalars are ignored -- av ties A to the true wiring."""
364	    ap = [pow(int(alpha), k, q) for k in range(6 + Lv + 2 * Lr)]
365	    U, R, Qv = scal["U"], scal["R"], scal["Qv"]
366	    val = ap[1] * ((U * av + R - X) % q) % q
367	    val = (val + ap[2] * ((av - 1 - R - Qv) % q)) % q
368	    su = U
369	    for j in range(Lv):
370	        su = (su - pow(2, Lv - 1 - j, q) * scal[f"Ub{j}"]) % q
371	    val = (val + ap[3] * su) % q
372	    sr = R
373	    for j in range(Lr):
374	        sr = (sr - pow(2, Lr - 1 - j, q) * scal[f"Rb{j}"]) % q
375	    val = (val + ap[4] * sr) % q
376	    sq = Qv
377	    for j in range(Lr):
378	        sq = (sq - pow(2, Lr - 1 - j, q) * scal[f"Qb{j}"]) % q
379	    val = (val + ap[5] * sq) % q
380	    c = 6
381	    for nm in ([f"Ub{j}" for j in range(Lv)]
382	               + [f"Rb{j}" for j in range(Lr)]
383	               + [f"Qb{j}" for j in range(Lr)]):
384	        T = scal[nm]
385	        val = (val + ap[c] * ((T - T * T) % q)) % q
386	        c += 1
387	    return val % q

390	def verify_constraints(W, rng, stats, q=DEFAULT_Q):
391	    """Degree-3 zero-test certifying u_d = floor(X/a_d) for the whole batch
392	    over F_q. Returns ok. (W["tabs"] must already be materialised over q;
393	    build_witness/rematerialize do this.)"""
394	    Lv, Lr, m = W["Lv"], W["Lr"], W["m"]
395	    X, p, dstart = W["X"], W["p"], W["dstart"]
396	    tau = [int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(m)]
397	    alpha = int(rng.integers(2, q))
398	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
399	    tabs = dict(W["tabs"])
400	    tabs["EQ"] = eq_table(tau, q)
401	    terms = build_terms(Lv, Lr, X, alpha, q)
402	    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
403	    ok, r_A, finalA, scal = sumcheck(0, tabs, terms, 3, rng, q)
404	    stats["comm"] += 4 * m                                  # degree-3 round polys
405	    if not ok:
406	        return False
407	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
408	    av = a_tilde(r_A, p, dstart, q)
409	    eqv = eq_point(tau, r_A, q)
410	    expect = eqv * constraint_eval(scal, av, X, Lv, Lr, alpha, q) % q
411	    res = (finalA % q) == expect
412	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
413	    return res

420	def honest_C(W, S_tab, rho, q):
421	    eqr = eq_table(rho, q)
422	    return _asum((eqr * S_tab[W["u"]]) % q, q)

425	def build_omega(W, rho, q):
426	    eqr = eq_table(rho, q)
427	    omega = np.zeros(1 << W["Lv"], dtype=_dt(q))
428	    np.add.at(omega, W["u"], eqr)            # < D summands each < q
429	    return omega % q

432	def verify_lookup(W, S_tab, rho, claimedC, omega, rng, stats, q):
433	    """B1 then B2; leaf claims on S / Ub_j closed by direct MLE opening."""
434	    Lv, m = W["Lv"], W["m"]
435	    # B1: claimedC = sum_v S(v) omega(v)
436	    okB1, r_B, finalB1, sB1 = sumcheck(claimedC,
437	                                       {"S": S_tab.copy(), "W": omega.copy()},
438	                                       [(1, ["S", "W"])], 2, rng, q)
439	    stats["comm"] += 3 * Lv
440	    if not okB1:
441	        return False
442	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
443	    okf = (finalB1 % q) == sB1["S"] * sB1["W"] % q
444	    okf = okf and sB1["S"] == mle_eval(S_tab, r_B, q)       # opening of S
445	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
446	    if not okf:
447	        return False
448	    sW = sB1["W"]                                           # claim for B2
449	    # B2: sW = sum_d eq(rho,d) prod_j EB_j(d),  EB_j = eq(r_B[j], Ub_j)
450	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
451	    tabs = {"EQrho": eq_table(rho, q)}
452	    ebnames = []
453	    for j in range(Lv):
454	        rb = int(r_B[j]) % q
455	        Ub = W["tabs"][f"Ub{j}"]
456	        EB = (((1 - rb) % q) + ((2 * rb - 1) % q) * Ub) % q
457	        nm = f"EB{j}"
458	        tabs[nm] = EB.astype(_dt(q))
459	        ebnames.append(nm)
460	    stats["t_prover"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
461	    okB2, r_C, finalB2, _ = sumcheck(sW, tabs, [(1, ["EQrho"] + ebnames)],
462	                                     Lv + 1, rng, q)
463	    stats["comm"] += (Lv + 2) * m
464	    if not okB2:
465	        return False
466	    t0 = time.perf_counter()
467	    expect = eq_point(rho, r_C, q)
468	    for j in range(Lv):
469	        rb = int(r_B[j]) % q
470	        ub = mle_eval(W["tabs"][f"Ub{j}"], r_C, q)         # opening of Ub_j
471	        ebj = (((1 - rb) % q) + ((2 * rb - 1) % q) * ub) % q
472	        expect = expect * ebj % q
473	    res = (finalB2 % q) == expect
474	    stats["t_verifier"] += time.perf_counter() - t0
475	    return res

482	def run_primitive(X, p, m, dstart, rng, q=DEFAULT_Q, S_seed=0, cheat=None):
483	    """Build the trace, the lookup claim, optionally corrupt, run both the
484	    constraint zero-test and the lookup over F_q. Returns dict(accepted, ...)."""
485	    W = build_witness(X, p, m, dstart, q)
486	    Lv = W["Lv"]
487	    S_tab = (np.random.default_rng(S_seed).integers(0, min(q, 1 << 62),
488	             size=1 << Lv) % q).astype(_dt(q))
489	    rho = [int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(m)]
490	    C = honest_C(W, S_tab, rho, q)
491	    omega = build_omega(W, rho, q)
492	    claimedC = C
493	
494	    if cheat == "u_consistent":          # self-consistent wrong quotient
495	        d = 1 % W["D"]
496	        nu = int(W["u"][d]) + 1
497	        W["tabs"]["U"] = W["tabs"]["U"].copy(); W["tabs"]["U"][d] = nu % q
498	        for j in range(Lv):
499	            W["tabs"][f"Ub{j}"] = W["tabs"][f"Ub{j}"].copy()
500	            W["tabs"][f"Ub{j}"][d] = (nu >> (Lv - 1 - j)) & 1
501	    elif cheat == "u_value":             # quotient off, bits untouched
502	        d = 1 % W["D"]
503	        W["tabs"]["U"] = W["tabs"]["U"].copy()
504	        W["tabs"]["U"][d] = (int(W["tabs"]["U"][d]) + 1) % q
505	    elif cheat == "r_value":             # remainder corrupted
506	        d = 1 % W["D"]
507	        W["tabs"]["R"] = W["tabs"]["R"].copy()
508	        W["tabs"]["R"][d] = (int(W["tabs"]["R"][d]) + 1) % q
509	    elif cheat == "nonbit":              # a 'bit' set to 2
510	        W["tabs"]["Ub0"] = W["tabs"]["Ub0"].copy()
511	        W["tabs"]["Ub0"][0] = 2
512	    elif cheat == "wrong_C":             # lie about the claimed value
513	        claimedC = (C + 1) % q
514	    elif cheat == "omega_route":         # corrupt routing, keep <S,omega>=C
515	        omega = omega.copy()
516	        omega[0] = (int(omega[0]) + 1) % q
517	        omega[-1] = (int(omega[-1]) - 1) % q
518	    elif cheat == "u_alias":             # wrap-around: u'' aliases X mod q
519	        W2, info = forge_alias(W, q)
520	        if W2 is not None:               # only constructible while q < X
521	            rematerialize(W2, q)
522	            W = W2
523	            # honest lookup keeps the true u (only the trace is forged) ->
524	            # this isolates the constraint test, the seat of the hole
525	            C = honest_C(W, S_tab, rho, q)
526	            omega = build_omega(W, rho, q)
527	            claimedC = C
528	
529	    stats = {"t_prover": 0.0, "t_verifier": 0.0, "comm": 0}
530	    okC = verify_constraints(W, rng, stats, q)
531	    okL = verify_lookup(W, S_tab, rho, claimedC, omega, rng, stats, q)
532	    return dict(accepted=(okC and okL), okC=okC, okL=okL, D=W["D"],
533	                Lv=Lv, Lr=W["Lr"], m=m, trueC=C, **stats)

537	# F_{q^2} refutation: an extension field does NOT lift the integer range
538	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
539	
540	class GF2:
541	    """F_{q^2} = F_q[t]/(t^2 + 1), valid when q % 4 == 3 (so -1 is a
542	    quadratic non-residue). Element a + b*t. Characteristic is q."""
543	    __slots__ = ("a", "b", "q")
544	
545	    def __init__(self, a, b, q):
546	        self.a = a % q
547	        self.b = b % q
548	        self.q = q
549	
550	    def __add__(s, o):
551	        return GF2(s.a + o.a, s.b + o.b, s.q)
552	
553	    def __sub__(s, o):
554	        return GF2(s.a - o.a, s.b - o.b, s.q)
555	
556	    def __mul__(s, o):                            # t^2 = -1
557	        q = s.q
558	        return GF2((s.a * o.a - s.b * o.b) % q, (s.a * o.b + s.b * o.a) % q, q)
559	
560	    def __eq__(s, o):
561	        return isinstance(o, GF2) and s.a == o.a and s.b == o.b
562	
563	    def is_zero(s):
564	        return s.a == 0 and s.b == 0
565	
566	    def __repr__(s):
567	        return f"({s.a}+{s.b}t)"
568	
569	    @staticmethod
570	    def embed(x, q):
571	        return GF2(x % q, 0, q)
572	
573	    @staticmethod
574	    def rand(rng, q):
575	        return GF2(int(rng.integers(0, q)), int(rng.integers(0, q)), q)
576	
577	
578	def _eqw_sum_c1(W, embed, eq_of, zero, tau, X):
579	    """Compute  sum_e eq(tau, e) * c1(e),  c1(e) = U[e]*A[e] + R[e] - X,
580	    directly over a field given by (embed, multiply/add via field objects,
581	    eq_of(tau,e), additive zero). This is EXACTLY the quantity the constraint
582	    zero-test certifies equals 0 for the multiply identity; the other
583	    constraints (bitness, recompositions, remainder bound) are satisfied as
584	    EXACT integers by the alias forgery, hence 0 in every field. So this sum
585	    is the whole soundness question for the wrap-around."""
586	    D = W["D"]
587	    u, a, r = W["u"], W["a"], W["r"]
588	    eX = embed(X)
589	    total = zero
590	    for e in range(D):
591	        c1 = embed(int(u[e])) * embed(int(a[e])) + embed(int(r[e])) - eX
592	        total = total + eq_of(tau, e) * c1
593	    return total
594

596	def refute_q2(n=33, p=7, m=4, seed=0, q0=DEFAULT_Q):
597	    """Demonstrate that the extension field F_{q0^2} CANNOT detect the
598	    wrap-around alias, while a true larger prime can. Builds an alias forgery
599	    against the base prime q0 (needs X > q0, so n > 31 for q0 = 2^31-1) and
600	    evaluates the multiply-identity zero-test over three fields."""
601	    assert q0 % 4 == 3, "GF2 with t^2=-1 needs q0 % 4 == 3"
602	    X = (1 << n) - 1
603	    dstart = max(1, int(X ** 0.5) // p + 1)
604	    W = build_witness(X, p, m, dstart, q=q0)
605	    W2, info = forge_alias(W, q0)
606	    assert W2 is not None, f"no alias fits at n={n}; raise n above log2(q0)"
607	    e0 = info["e0"]
608	
609	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
610	    # the integer the forged entry violates the multiply identity by:
611	    delta = info["k"] * q0                              # u''*a+r'' - X = k*q0
612	
613	    out = {"info": info, "delta": delta}
614	
615	    # --- F_{q0}: the base prime (too small) -- aliases to zero ---
616	    # (the prime path accumulates unreduced ints; reduce at the end, since
617	    #  mod is a ring homomorphism -> this is exactly the field sum)
618	    tau_p = [int(rng.integers(0, q0)) for _ in range(m)]
619	    sp = _eqw_sum_c1(W2, lambda x: x % q0,
620	                     lambda t, e: _eq_bool_prime(t, e, m, q0),
621	                     0, tau_p, X)
622	    out["base_prime_sum"] = sp % q0                      # 0 -> undetected
623	
624	    # --- F_{q0^2}: the EXTENSION field -- challenges drawn from all of F_{q0^2} ---
625	    tau_g = [GF2.rand(rng, q0) for _ in range(m)]
626	    sg = _eqw_sum_c1(W2, lambda x: GF2.embed(x, q0),
627	                     lambda t, e: _eq_bool_gf2(t, e, m, q0),
628	                     GF2(0, 0, q0), tau_g, X)
629	    out["ext_field_sum"] = sg                           # (0,0) -> undetected
630	
631	    # --- F_Q: a genuine larger prime (Q > X + k*q0) -- detects it ---
632	    Q = BIG_Q
633	    assert Q > X + delta
634	    tau_b = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(m)]
